key_insight: A constitutive artificial neural network discovered a compact, interpretable hyperelastic strain-energy function for veins that captures biaxial mechanical behavior better than standard vein models.
engineering_relevance: This provides a data-driven constitutive law that could improve simulation and design for vein grafts, arteriovenous fistulas, and tissue-engineered vascular grafts.
method: Fit a CANN to biaxial stress-stretch data from saphenous, jugular, and inferior vena cava veins.
Expand the candidate function library with terms for fiber recruitment and fiber-family interactions.
Use Sobol sensitivity analysis, correlation pruning, and response-level family collapse to reduce the model to an 8-term SEF.
evidence_signal: The final eight-term strain-energy function achieved higher accuracy than established venous constitutive models across all three vein types, with R² > 0.9 and p < 0.01.
watch_item: The proposed constitutive form should be validated on larger, independent cohorts before broad clinical or design use.
paper_title: Data-Driven Discovery of a Hyperelastic Strain-Energy Function for Veins Using Constitutive Artificial Neural Networks
